CHEAP_DATA_NOW: Current public EDGX rulebook documents the <=390 equity orders/day monthly-average retail-priority limit and parent/child counting. No public/free fill data qualified with retail flag, queue position and matched ordinary-control orders.
CHEAP_EXPRESSION: Fixed eligible low-frequency displayed order at an existing price; compare fill/adverse-selection economics against same-price ordinary priority. Cannot infer fills from daily OHLC or public aggregate BBO.
ECONOMIC_SIGNIFICANCE: Queue preference is a plausible low-scale structural rent, but no measurable free-data expression is ready.
FAILED_CRITERIA: Free attributed queue/fill/markout data and proven eligible access.
FATAL_PROBLEM: RMO certification/routing, order-origin rules, queue-level attribution and execution/adverse-selection observations cannot be established from public daily data. No broker interaction or live orders are authorized.
LESSON: Do not backtest a private matching flag from aggregate prices, or confuse order-frequency qualification with account access.
MECHANISM: EDGX gives qualified Retail Priority Orders structural queue preference over ordinary same-price interest, allowing a genuinely small order source to earn a matching priority unavailable to institutional flow.
NEXT_DECISION: New public attributed retail-priority dataset/access documentation required. Next L0 transferable subscription rights forced liquidation; inspect existing rights qualification first.
UNCERTAINTY: Rulebook advantage exists; broker eligibility and net benefit unknown.
WHO_PAYS: Ordinary queued suppliers lose time-priority/fills; liquidity takers pay the spread. Priority alone does not guarantee positive adverse-selection-adjusted PnL.
WHY_PERSIST: Exchange defines retail certification and low order-frequency eligibility; brokers/RMOs control the eligible routing path, limiting scale and direct access.
